title: Compressor fouling after haze season
symptoms: T30 and T50 rising slowly over about 40 cycles, P30 falling, W31 and W32 falling, core speed creeping up.
root_cause: Heavy compressor blade fouling. Inlet filter differential pressure was high and one filter stage was damaged.
actions: Replaced damaged inlet filter stage, performed offline crank wash. Temperatures and pressures returned close to baseline.
outcome: Resolved. Online wash frequency increased during haze season.

title: Repeat fouling, wash only partly effective
symptoms: HPC degradation pattern: T24, T30, T50 rising, P30 falling, Ps30 rising. Online wash gave only small improvement.
root_cause: Fouling plus early blade tip erosion found on borescope inspection of rear HPC stages.
actions: Offline wash, borescope inspection, erosion logged for monitoring. Blade replacement planned for major overhaul.
outcome: Partly resolved. Unit monitored with tighter thresholds.

title: False alarm from failed T30 thermocouple
symptoms: Sudden 6 degR step in T30 with no change in P30, T50 or speeds.
actions: Instrumentation work order, thermocouple replaced, calibration checked.

title: Bleed valve stuck partly open
symptoms: P30 and engine pressure ratio dropping with T30 stable. htBleed rising.
root_cause: Compressor bleed valve actuator stuck partly open.
actions: Actuator overhauled and position feedback recalibrated.

title: Cooling air blockage caught early
symptoms: W31 falling quickly over 8 cycles while other sensors were stable.
root_cause: Debris partially blocking an HPT cooling air passage.
actions: Escalated to engineer, unit taken offline, passage cleared, borescope of HPT first stage blades found no damage.

title: Late detection of fouling led to forced outage
symptoms: HPC degradation pattern noticed only when T50 neared its alarm level.
root_cause: Advanced compressor fouling missed in manual trend reviews.
actions: Forced outage, offline wash, borescope inspection.
outcome: Resolved. Review found the trend was visible about 50 cycles earlier.

title: Exhaust spread from fuel nozzle wear
symptoms: T50 rising faster than T30, exhaust thermocouple spread widening.
root_cause: Two worn fuel nozzles creating a hot spot.
actions: Fuel nozzles replaced at planned stop, hot gas path borescope showed minor coating loss.

title: Bearing vibration with speed drift
symptoms: Core speed drifting with normal temperatures and pressures, bearing vibration trending up.
root_cause: Early bearing wear confirmed by lube oil wear metal analysis.
actions: Escalated, load reduced by engineer, bearing replaced at planned stop.
